title: Request: interpret knitr option `fig.path` the same as knitr
description:
The knitr option `fig.path` can specify a directory and a file prefix together. E.g., a standard value in `README.Rmd` files in packages is `fig.path = "man/figures/README-"`, which means put plots in the `man/figures/` directory and prefix the file names with `README-`.

However, asciicast interprets `fig.path` as just a directory name. So in the example above it would create a new directory named `man/figures/README-/`, and then place its output files there without the `README-` prefix.

Here's a minimal example of an R Markdown file:

````markdown
---
output: github_document
---

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.path = "man/figures/README-",
  out.width = "100%"
)

asciicast::init_knitr_engine()
```

Regular R plot:

```{r}
#| label: rplot

plot(pressure)
```

asciicast:

```{asciicast}
#| label: ascii-fig

cat("\033[31mHello world\033[0m\n")
```

````

The saved figures are then
 * `man/figures/README-rplot-1.png`
 * `man/figures/README-/ascii-fig.svg`

I request that asciicast interpret `fig.path` the same as knitr so that the latter file would instead be `man/figures/README-ascii-fig.svg`.

Thanks for your consideration.

title: Hand-crafted casts
description:
For the purpose of snapshot testing in pillar and other packages, I'd like to quickly render predefined output to SVG. I imagine this is also useful for rendering.

How do you feel about exposing a constructor for an output-only cast that consists of a single frame?

Example (with GIF rendering because SVG didn't work in a reprex).

``` r
out <- capture.output({
  options(cli.num_colors = 256)
  print(tibble::tibble(a = 1))
})

writeLines(out)
#> [38;5;246m# A tibble: 1 × 1[39m
#>       a
#>   [3m[38;5;246m<dbl>[39m[23m
#> [38;5;250m1[39m     1

output <- tibble::tibble(time = 0, type = "o", data = paste0(out, "\r\n"))

height <- length(out) + 1
width <- max(utf8::utf8_width(fansi::strip_sgr(out)))

config <- list(
  version = 2L,
  command = "cat",
  timestamp = as.integer(Sys.time()),
  env = list(TERM = "xterm-256color", SHELL = "/bin/zsh"),
  height = height,
  rows = height,
  width = width,
  cols = width
)

cast <- asciicast:::new_cast(config, output)

# GIF output for the purpose of the reprex
# The target is SVG
suppressMessages(asciicast::write_gif(cast, path = "cast.gif"))

knitr::include_graphics("cast.gif")
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/QO3jEju.gif)<!-- -->

<sup>Created on 2025-03-26 with [reprex v2.1.1](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>

title: Tailoring Typing Speed and Inter-Code Waiting Intervals
description:
Impressive project!

Would it be possible to incorporate a parameter for adjusting typing speed and the waiting interval between "code chunks"? This feature could enable faster typing in specific sections and a more deliberate pace in others, catering to the need for additional time to comprehend specific outputs.

title: Missing output with `vctrs` classes
description:
`asciicast` does not include all output for `vctrs` classes. Specifically, it doesn't include the line displaying the class. Here's an R Markdown reprex, along with the output.

````
---
title: "reprex"
output: github_document
always_allow_html: true
---

```{r, include = FALSE, cache = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.path = "man/figures/README-",
  out.width = "100%",
  cache = FALSE,
  asciicast_theme = "pkgdown"
)
asciicast::init_knitr_engine(
  echo = TRUE,
  echo_input = FALSE
)
```

`asciicast` does not include all output for `vctrs` classes. For example, if we run the following in an `r` code chunk we get:

```{r}
library(clock)
x <- year_month_day(2019, 2, 1)
add_months(x, 1)
```

But the `asciicast` code chunk does not include the first line containing `<year_month_day<day>[1]>`:

```{asciicast}
library(clock)
x <- year_month_day(2019, 2, 1)
add_months(x, 1)
```

````

title: Parameters are messed up, especially in knitr
description:
There are many ways to set parameters, and it is not entirely clear what the best way is.

The knitr engine is especially messy. E.g. you can pass `options` to `init_knitr_engine()` and these are added as `R.options` chunk options, but then if you specify `R.options` for a chunk that overrides all of them. Really weird.

It is also hard to specify options to asciicast in Rd/roxygen2. cli has a working example, but it is not pleasant at all.

title: Move `master` branch to `main`
description:
The `master` branch of this repository will soon be renamed to `main`, as part of a coordinated change across several GitHub organizations (including, but not limited to: [tidyverse](https://github.com/tidyverse), [r-lib](https://github.com/r-lib), [tidymodels](https://github.com/tidymodels), and [sol-eng](https://github.com/sol-eng)). We anticipate this will happen by the end of September 2021.

That will be preceded by a release of the [usethis package](https://usethis.r-lib.org), which will gain some functionality around detecting and adapting to a renamed default branch. There will also be a blog post at the time of this `master` --> `main` change.

The purpose of this issue is to:

* Help us firm up the list of targetted repositories
* Make sure all maintainers are aware of what's coming
* Give us an issue to close when the job is done
* Give us a place to put advice for collaborators re: how to adapt

*message id: euphoric_snowdog*
